Built by former SentinelOne, Wiz, and Palo Alto Networks veterans, Neo gives SecOps teams the inventory, posture intelligence, attribution, and policy control to manage enterprise-wide agentic transformation and secure AI agents, AI-enabled applications, browsers, identities, and traditional software with newly introduced agentic capabilities. Neo will use the capital to rapidly scale its go-to-market and engineering teams as enterprises prioritize security initiatives to manage rapid agentic software adoption. “Enterprise security was built for a world where software behaved predictably,” said Nick Warner, CEO and Co-Founder of Neo. “That world is changing fast. AI agents and agentic capabilities are being embedded into browsers, developer tools, SaaS platforms, and traditional applications, giving software the ability to reason, act, invoke tools, and move through workflows with valid user permissions. Neo gives enterprises the real-time control layer they need to understand what agentic software can do, govern how it behaves, and secure adoption without slowing down the business.” Agentic adoption is changing enterprise environments faster than traditional security programs can adapt. Threat surfaces are shifting and mutating as employees adopt new AI tools from the bottom up, while established software vendors add agentic capabilities into products already approved for enterprise use. As a result, SecOps teams are being asked to secure autonomous software operating inside approved business applications, often without the visibility and control necessary to govern its behavior. According to Gartner, only 5% of enterprise applications featured agentic capabilities in 2025, but 40% will by the end of 2026. Neo addresses this gap by introducing a real-time control layer for evolving software stacks, helping SecOps teams inventory the suite of tools running across the enterprise even as they add new agentic functions, understand their changing capabilities and risks, assess whether they are configured safely, and enforce policy before risky activity occurs. “Enterprise software is becoming agentic, changing how applications behave, what they can access, and how work gets done,” said Zane Lackey, General Partner at Andreessen Horowitz. “Employees are rapidly adopting AI agents and software vendors are embedding agentic capabilities into products enterprises already use. Organizations need visibility into what this software can do and the ability to govern its behavior in real time. Nick, Shlomi, Eran, and the Neo team have built category-defining security platforms before, and we believe they’re uniquely positioned to build the control layer this new generation of enterprise software requires.” Existing security architectures were built for a different model of enterprise software, comprised of deterministic applications, human users, and known paths of data movement. Agentic systems behave differently. They can act independently, mimic user behavior, inherit permissions, chain tools, and move across workflows in ways that appear legitimate to security tools built for earlier eras of software. Securing this new model requires real-time visibility into both human and non-human activity, attribution that maps actions back to the responsible user or agent, and granular policy enforcement inside the software layer where agentic activity occurs. “Agentic AI is creating a new security category as enterprise environments transform, becoming largely composed of software that can reason, act, and invoke tools on its own,” said Elliott Robinson, Partner at Bessemer Venture Partners. “Neo combines a clear architectural view of how to control this new software layer with a founding team that has built enterprise-grade security platforms at scale before. That combination matters in a crowded market. Vision is important, but execution will determine the companies that define this next era of security, and Neo is tackling one of agentic security’s hardest problems.” The Neo Platform delivers five core capabilities Neoverse-Powered Software Inventory: SecOps teams receive a full inventory of AI agents, AI-enabled applications, plugins, extensions, MCP servers, and traditional software becoming agentic, enriched by Neoverse, Neo’s continuously updated knowledge base of agentic software capabilities, risks, and behaviors. Capability and Risk Intelligence: Neo helps teams understand what agentic and non-agentic software can do, what it can access, and whether it is configured safely. Real-Time Attribution: Each action prod

jobs.title: Director, NA Field Marketing Marketing Remote View Role
jobs.description: Neo Security is looking for a Director of Field Marketing & Events to build and lead our field marketing function from the ground up. You will own the strategy and execution of everything that puts our brand and our team in front of prospects and customers in person and virtually: conferences, executive roundtables, regional field events, our own user summit, and sponsorships. You'll partner closely with Sales, Sales Development, and Product Marketing to turn pipeline and revenue targets into a calendar of high-impact programs, and you'll be the person in the room ensuring every event ties back to measurable pipeline and brand outcomes. This is a player-coach role for someone who has run field marketing in a fast-moving B2B security or infrastructure software company, is comfortable owning a budget and a number, and enjoys both the strategic planning and the on-the-ground execution of events. What You'll Do • Own the field marketing strategy and calendar across regions, including third-party conferences (e.g., RSA, Black Hat, Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit), industry roundtables, executive dinners, regional meetups, and Neo Security's flagship user/customer event. • Build and manage the field marketing budget, allocating spend across sponsorships, owned events, and travel to maximize pipeline contribution and ROI. • Partner with Sales and SDR leadership to align event and field programs with territory plans, target account lists, and pipeline goals. • Design and execute account-based marketing (ABM) programs and integrated regional campaigns in partnership with Demand Generation and Product Marketing. • Manage vendor and sponsorship relationships, negotiating contracts and evaluating conference ROI to inform future investment. • Lead event logistics end-to-end: venue selection, booth/space design, staffing, swag and collateral, speaker sessions, and on-site execution. • Define and report on field marketing KPIs (pipeline sourced/influenced, cost per meeting, cost per opportunity, event attendance and conversion) and present results to marketing and sales leadership. • Build and manage a team of field marketers and/or event coordinators as the program scales, including contractors and agencies for peak event seasons. • Represent the marketing function at key industry events, occasionally including public-facing or spokesperson duties. • Stay current on the cybersecurity conference and analyst landscape to identify new, high-value opportunities for visibility. Requirements • 8+ years in field marketing, event marketing, or demand generation, with at least 3 years in a leadership or head-of-function role. • Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally in cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, or another technical/enterprise IT space. • Proven track record designing field programs that generate measurable pipeline, with fluency in pipeline attribution and marketing ROI reporting. • Hands-on experience managing large-scale industry conferences and sponsorships (booth strategy, speaking slots, executive briefings). • Strong budget management skills, including vendor negotiation and cost/ROI tracking across a multi-hundred-thousand-dollar annual events budget. • Experience partnering closely with Sales leadership and working from a shared pipeline/revenue targets model. • Proficiency with marketing and sales tools such as Salesforce, a marketing automation platform (e.g., HubSpot, Marketo), and event management/registration tools. • Excellent project management skills and the ability to run multiple concurrent events and workstreams without dropping details. • Willingness to travel domestically up to 30-40%, including some evenings/weekends around major industry events. • Based in the United States, able to work across U.S. time zones. Nice to Haves • Experience marketing to security, IT, or DevOps buyer personas (CISOs, security engineers, IT admins). • Familiarity with the cybersecurity conference circuit and analyst ecosystem (Gartner, Forrester) and existing relationships with sponsors/organizers. • Experience building a field marketing function from an early stage at a startup or scale-up (Series B–D or equivalent). • Experience running executive-level programs, such as CISO advisory boards, dinners, or invite-only briefings. • Background in partner or channel marketing events. • Familiarity with ABM platforms (e.g., 6sense, Demandbase) and integrating field programs into ABM plays. • Creative eye for booth design, event branding, and on-site experience.

jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer - Browser Extension R&D Tel Aviv View Role
jobs.description: About the Role We're looking for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to join our engineering team. You'll work on our Chrome extension, a core part of our security platform that runs on managed endpoints across the enterprise and operates in the browser in real time. You'll own Neo's policy enforcement engine in the browser, the layer that turns security policies into real-time decisions on every page users visit. Additionally, you'll also build features across our backend services and web app. What You'll Do • Architect, build, and maintain our Chrome extension • Own features from design through production monitoring. • Debug hard problems across the browser, the OS, and the backend. • Help shape the product's technical direction and raise the bar on code quality, testing, and release practices. • Build in-browser security capabilities: DOM inspection and manipulation, user-facing warning and blocking flows, and event capture. • Keep the extension fast and invisible. Minimize page-load impact, memory footprint, and CPU usage on every site. • Drive support for other Chromium browsers (Edge, Brave) and, over time, Firefox and Safari WebExtensions. • Manage Chrome extension publishing, versioning, and staged rollouts. • Build and extend the APIs and services that power the extension, including configuration delivery, real-time updates. • Build features in our React/TypeScript web app that let customers configure the product, review events, and manage deployments. jobs.title: Senior Low Level Engineer - Infrastructure R&D Tel Aviv View Role
jobs.description: Senior Low Level Engineer - Infrastructure About the Role Build the agent that Neo's whole product depends on: a privileged, cross-platform systems program written in Rust. Everything Neo shows a security team starts on the endpoint. The sensor is the organization's presence on each machine - responsible for collection, posture and visibility, and local enforcement of the organization's security policies. Doing that well means running deep in the operating system on Windows, macOS and Linux: always on, trusted with elevated access, and never in the way. This role owns the hard parts of it. What you'll work on • The low-level, OS-level infrastructure the sensor is built on: the layer that handles low-level and OS-level operations directly and turns raw platform capabilities into reliable building blocks for everything above it - installation and deployment, endpoint security frameworks, network visibility, driver-adjacent work and more. • Infrastructure that is the backbone of the product — code where stability, correctness, and quality aren't aspirations but the actual job, because every feature Neo ships stands on it. • The sensor's core capabilities on top of that foundation: collection, posture and visibility, and local enforcement of the organization's security policies. • Reliability engineering for software that can't fail quietly: crash handling, recovery, and keeping the agent healthy and hard to tamper with on machines no one is watching. • The full lifecycle of a production system agent: how it ships, installs, updates, and runs unattended across a customer fleet. Tech you'll work with The work is low-level systems development in Rust, close to the operating system across Windows, macOS, and Linux - memory, processes, files, networking and the OS internals that expose them. Alongside that, you'll lean hard on agentic coding tools; deep fluency with at least one is central to how we work, not a bonus. Expect to range across the stack - OS internals, AI tooling internals, CI, and a fair amount of reverse engineering - and to learn the parts you don't know yet. What we're looking for • 5+ years of systems programming in Rust, C, or C++, working close to the OS. • Hands-on experience with the internals of at least one of Windows, macOS or Linux (services or daemons, process and file APIs, security frameworks and low level development). • Experience shipping and operating production-grade software for a large customer base - you understand what enterprise-grade means in practice: reliability across thousands of diverse environments, upgrades that can't break anyone, and problems you only ever see through telemetry • Strong ownership and independence - you drive your work end to end, stay independent without going dark, and keep the customer's experience in view even when you're ten layers deep in the OS. • A team player with strong communication skills - you explain deep technical work clearly, surface problems and discuss them, resolve technical disagreements with arguments rather than ego, and make the people around you better. Nice to have • A security background - endpoint protection, EDR/MDM, or any product whose job is defending machines rather than just running on them. • Networking - protocols, secure transport, and how software behaves on real-world networks; hands-on experience with traffic inspection, interception, or network visibility tooling is a real plus. • Deeper AI knowledge - beyond daily tool use: how models and agents work under the hood, or experience building agentic workflows and evaluating their output. • Applied cryptography - you've worked with encryption, signing, or trust chains in real systems, not just used a library blindly. • Backend / Full stack knowledge and understanding.

jobs.description: About the Role Own the pipeline that turns raw endpoint telemetry into security intelligence. You'll work at the core of Neo: the ingestion and enrichment path that takes reports from tens of thousands of endpoints, extracts and deduplicates software, and runs an AI research pipeline that classifies and risk-scores every tool. You'll design the data model, the public API our dashboard and customers depend on, and the auth and identity layer that ties it all to real organizations. What you'll work on • The event-driven ingestion pipeline: S3 uploads → Lambda processors → Postgres, with idempotent processing, stale-work reaping, and back-pressure at scale. • The AI enrichment and researcher system — orchestrating LLM-backed agents, handling contradictions, and keeping cost and latency in check. • The public REST API (Hono), its typed schemas, and the generated clients that consume it. • Authentication, SSO/SAML federation, and multi-tenant identity and authorization. • Data modeling and schema evolution you can ship without downtime. Tech you'll work with TypeScript on Node 24 · Hono · AWS Lambda, API Gateway, EventBridge, SQS, S3, Cognito · Aurora Serverless v2 Postgres with Drizzle ORM · RDS Proxy · Pulumi (IaC) · pnpm monorepo · GitHub Actions · zod · pino · OpenAPI-generated clients · Sentry · an MCP server exposing the API to agents. What we're looking for • 6+ years building and operating production backend systems, ideally distributed or event-driven on a major cloud (AWS a strong plus). • Deep SQL and relational data modeling — you think in terms of indexes, transactions, and safe schema migrations, and you've been burned by a bad one and learned from it. • Strong API design instincts and a bias for typed, contract-first interfaces. • Comfortable owning reliability and observability for the services you build. • Fluent — or eager to become fluent — with agentic coding tools as a force multiplier. jobs.description: Accessibility Statement | Neo Skip to content Neo Launches with $100M to Secure AI Software Across the Enterprise Why Neo Platform Resources Company Get a Demo Toggle menu Resources Explore the agentic threat surface through research, field notes, and practical tools. Newsroom Neo Launches With $100M Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer back the agentic software control company. Library Blog Research & field notes Exposure Calculator Quantify your agent risk Newsroom News Press & announcements Company An AI-native team building the control layer for an AI-native world. Hiring Build Neo With Us We are hiring across detection engineering and the field. Company About Mission & team Careers Open roles at Neo Contact Us Talk to our team Newsroom News Latest announcements Why Neo Platform Resources Library Blog Exposure Calculator Newsroom News Company Company About Careers Contact Us Newsroom News Get a Demo Legal Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making Neo usable by everyone, how our web surfaces conform with WCAG 2.2 Level AA, and how to tell us when something falls short. On this page Scope Conformance Status Measures We Take Assessment Approach Third-Party Content Compatibility With Browsers and Assistive Technology Technical Specifications Feedback and Reporting a Barrier Changes to This Statement Neo Security, Inc. (“Neo,” “we,” or “us”) is committed to making its web surfaces accessible to the widest possible audience, regardless of ability or technology. We treat accessibility as a build requirement rather than a remediation phase: the people who design and build Neo are responsible for its accessibility, in the same change that ships the work. Scope This statement covers: the Neo website at https://www.neo.ai ; the Neo application at https://app.neo.security , including the customer dashboard for inventory, policies and activity, and the sign-in flow; and Neo customer documentation. These surfaces are covered in both light and dark themes. The content assessed is English-only, and the dashboard is designed for desktop use. Conformance Status The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) define requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. Neo supports WCAG 2.2 Level A and Level AA. Within the scope and reporting basis described in this statement, every applicable success criterion is recorded as “Supports” — meaning the functionality has at least one method that meets the criterion without known defects, or meets it with equivalent facilitation. Conformance is scoped for full pages and complete processes, as set out in the WCAG 2 Conformance Requirements . Neo maintains an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) covering this assessment, prepared on the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT®) version 2.5Rev, WCAG Edition. Customers and prospective customers can request the current report from accessibilitysupport@neo.ai . Measures We Take Accessibility requirements are written into the engineering standard Neo is built to, and are reviewed as part of the work rather than after it. In practice that means: Native semantics first. Interfaces are built from real HTML landmarks, headings, buttons, and links. Controls expose accessible names, roles, values and states; inputs use explicit labels and error associations. ARIA is added only where a native element cannot express the behaviour, because incorrect ARIA is worse than none. Keyboard operability. Navigation, search, policy controls, authentication and documentation can be operated by keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator and a logical focus order. Dialogs and panels can be entered and left with standard keyboard controls, and closing one returns focus to the invoking control or a logical fallback. Focus is never dropped, and is not obscured by overlays or fixed navigation. Pointer alternatives. Functionality can be completed with ordinary single-pointer interactions, without multi-point or path-based gestures. Where dragging is offered, an equivalent single-pointer control is provided alongside it. Reduced motion. Animation is gated behind the prefers-reduced-motion setting. Readers who ask their operating system to reduce motion receive a version with the motion removed, not merely shortened. Contrast and target size. Text meets a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1, and 3:1 for qualifying large text. Control boundaries, focus indicators and meaningful graphics meet 3:1. Pointer targets meet the minimum target-size requirement or an applicable spacing exception. Each threshold is checked in both themes. Reflow, resize and text spacing. Content remains usable at 320 CSS pixels or equivalent zoom without horizontal page scrolling, and text can be resized to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Text-spacing overrides can be applied in both themes without clipping. Wide data tables may scroll within their own containers where a two-dimensional presentation is necessary. Meaningful alternatives. Meaningful images, icons and charts have text alternatives or equivalent text and data presentations. Decorative imagery is hidden from assistive technology so it does not add noise. No information is available only as text embedded in an image. Status and errors. Search results, required-field feedback and form errors are announced through appropriate status or alert semantics, without requiring users to find the message manually. Correctable errors provide guidance, and destructive actions request confirmation and offer a cancel action. Assessment Approach Neo assesses accessibility by internal automated and manual evaluation, carried out by our engineering and product teams. Methods include automated accessibility test suites, AI-assisted checks, and manual keyboard and VoiceOver evaluation of major flows, together with targeted checks for text resize, reflow, text spacing, contrast, focus b
